message:
I wasn't able to run a quick sanity check with Python since Bash execution is blocked in this session (no approval surface available). The implementation itself is done, using only stdlib.

`slug.py` now implements `slugify` (no new definitions, no renames, satisfying both locks and the `AI NOTE` against third-party packages):

- `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` + ASCII encode/decode strips accents (`é` → `e`).
- Lowercases, then `re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ...)` collapses runs of non-alphanumerics into a single `-`.
- `.strip("-")` removes leading/trailing dashes, applied both before and after truncating to `max_length` (so a cut that lands mid-dash-run doesn't leave a trailing `-`).

diff --git a/slug.py b/slug.py
index d8e75c0..cad6456 100644
--- a/slug.py
+++ b/slug.py
@@ -1,5 +1,12 @@
 # AI NOTE: no third-party packages in this module
 
+import re
+import unicodedata
+
+
 def slugify(title: str, max_length: int = 60) -> str:
     # lowercase, accents stripped (é -> e), runs of non-alphanumerics -> one '-', no leading/trailing '-'
-    ...
+    normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title)
+    ascii_only = normalized.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
+    slug = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ascii_only.lower()).strip("-")
+    return slug[:max_length].strip("-")
